fixes.summary: _localize_takeoff_text()'s Japanese-mode phrase substitution was a case-sensitive, non-word-boundary str.replace() loop, so freely-worded item names imported from external AI-review data displayed as a garbled English/Japanese mashup, and English plurals left a stray 's' glued onto the translated Japanese word. Replaced with a case-insensitive, word-boundary-aware regex substitution plus a suffix-stripping pass and additional dictionary entries.

confirmed_shared_by_two_screens: module1's "不明・図面矛盾への回答" (unresolved/conflict review) dialog
known_residual_gaps: "Air-conditioning in扉 units" -- the "in扉" fragment's origin was not identified in this session and needs investigation of the AI-import canonicalization step, not just the dictionary

the English conjunction "and" is intentionally not translated standalone, to avoid affecting many existing correctly-working long phrase entries that already contain "and" as part of their whole-phrase match

new_self_checks.summary: Source-level check that _localize_takeoff_text() still uses re.IGNORECASE and a word-boundary regex, plus the plural-"s" stripping pass; behavioral check against known garbled test phrases. Verified to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fixed code.

verification.regression_of_regression_test_itself: Manually reverted both the regex mechanism and the suffix-stripping pass in a scratch copy and confirmed the new self-check fails as expected, then re-confirmed it passes on the fixed source.

structural_note: This is a finite hand-curated phrase dictionary trying to cover effectively unbounded freely-worded external AI item names. The fix closes the specific gaps found and the two mechanical bugs (case sensitivity, partial-word matching), but a genuinely new phrase from a future AI submission may still show up partially untranslated (cleanly in English, not garbled) until this dictionary-substitution architecture is replaced by a closed canonical vocabulary or a real translation engine.
